summary: Backend-only verification of the K8s/nginx health-probe fixes. All 12 pytest tests PASS in ~5s. Root-level GET /health returns 200 {status:'ok'} on localhost:8001 (which is where the K8s probe calls). Root-level GET / returns 200 {app:'Smart Kitchen AI', ok:true}. GET /api/ still returns the same body (unchanged). After `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`, /health became 200 in ~0.66s (well under the 3s target), confirming the startup no longer waits on DB index creation / storage init (they now run in a background asyncio task). No new traceback in backend.err.log since the last uvicorn boot. Regression smoke passed: signin with chef@cucina.ai works; /api/recipes, /api/pantry, /api/shopping, /api/household return 200; unique email index still enforced (duplicate signup -> 400); household invite_code created (6 chars) and lookup path works. NOTE: In this preview environment the external ingress routes non-/api paths to the Expo frontend (returns HTML on https://<preview>/health), so external-URL /health cannot be used to validate the FastAPI probe; the deployment probe uses cluster-internal http://<pod>:8001/health, which is what the tests assert.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: `app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, ...)` is registered AFTER `app.include_router(api_router)` and after the root-level /health and / handlers. In Starlette, middleware added after routes still applies globally, so functionally OK, but stylistically the middleware setup belongs before routes for clarity.
server.py is 1188 lines — well over the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into modules (auth, recipes, pantry, shopping, meals, ai, household, storage) for maintainability.
Legacy `@app.on_event('startup')` / 'shutdown' are deprecated in FastAPI; migrate to `lifespan` context manager. Non-blocking, but will emit a DeprecationWarning on newer FastAPI versions.

`_startup_tasks()` swallows index-creation exceptions with a warning log; that's fine for boot resilience, but the previous bcrypt-related traceback in backend.err.log (older boots) suggests a passlib+bcrypt version drift — the current boot no longer shows it, so nothing to fix now.
seed_data_creation: Idempotent: signup of chef@cucina.ai returns 400 if it already exists (which it does), then signin is used. One ephemeral TEST_iter10_<uuid> user was created for the household unique-code test and deleted via DELETE /api/auth/account in the same test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with `EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=<preview-url> pytest backend/tests/test_iter10_health_probes.py -n 0` — the restart test must run serially (it restarts uvicorn, which breaks any concurrent worker). pytest.ini forces `-n 2 --dist loadscope` by default, so pass `-n 0` to override. External https://<preview>/health returns HTML from Expo (ingress routing), which is expected in the preview cluster; production uses a different ingress that hits FastAPI directly, so validation is against http://localhost:8001/health.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. The PR under test correctly addresses the RCA described in the problem statement: (a) K8s/nginx probe hit /health (no /api prefix) and got 404 → fixed by adding a root-level @app.get('/health') handler outside the api_router; (b) startup was blocked on `db.*.create_index(...)` awaits and `init_storage()` HTTP calls before uvicorn began serving, so the probe timed out → fixed by moving those into `asyncio.create_task(_startup_tasks())` inside on_startup, so the port binds immediately and index/storage init happen in the background. Verified empirically: /health responds ~0.66s after `supervisorctl restart backend`.
